items.micro_skill: apply ARMA Rule 1 when indexing
items.stem:
Under ANSI/ARMA 12-2005, a clerk files these folders alphabetically. Which personal name goes FIRST?
Jose Manalo | Josefina Manalo | Joel Manalo | Jose Manalang

reveal.terms: Indexing writes a name as filing units: surname, given name, middle initial for people; words as written for businesses and organizations. Compare unit by unit, letter by letter.
reveal.shortcut: Rewrite each name in indexed form first, then sort the rewritten forms.
reveal.why_correct: "Jose Manalang" is filed first. Indexed order: MANALANG / JOSE; MANALO / JOEL; MANALO / JOSE; MANALO / JOSEFINA. Index each name into units and compare unit by unit, letter by letter; nothing comes before something (ARMA Rule 1). This follows the standard office filing rule (ARMA International Simplified Filing Standard Rules, Rule 1), not a rule published by the CSC. Source standard: ANSI/ARMA 12-2005.

why_wrong.o1: "Jose Manalo" indexes as MANALO / JOSE and files third, so it is not first. Picking it ignores this: compare unit by unit, letter by letter; nothing comes before something.
why_wrong.o2: "Joel Manalo" indexes as MANALO / JOEL and files second, so it is not first. Picking it ignores this: compare unit by unit, letter by letter; nothing comes before something.
why_wrong.o4: "Josefina Manalo" indexes as MANALO / JOSEFINA and files fourth, so it is not first. Picking it ignores this: compare unit by unit, letter by letter; nothing comes before something.

items.stem:
Folders are filed in ascending order of their number, read as a whole number (not digit by digit). Which folder is filed FIRST?
RF-1088 | RF-998 | RF-1080 | RF-10080

reveal.terms: Numeric filing orders records by the value of the number. A number with fewer digits is smaller, whatever its first digit.
reveal.shortcut: Count the digits first: fewer digits file earlier. Compare digit by digit only when the counts are equal.
reveal.why_correct: Ascending values: RF-998 (998); RF-1080 (1,080); RF-1088 (1,088); RF-10080 (10,080). So "RF-998" is first. Names that start with digits file before names that start with letters, in ascending order of value; ordinal endings are ignored (ARMA Rule 7). This follows the standard office filing rule (ARMA International Simplified Filing Standard Rules, Rule 7), not a rule published by the CSC.

why_wrong.o1: "RF-10080" has the value 10,080 and is number 4 of 4 in ascending order. Comparing digit by digit from the left puts it in the wrong place.
why_wrong.o3: "RF-1088" has the value 1,088 and is number 3 of 4 in ascending order. Comparing digit by digit from the left puts it in the wrong place.
why_wrong.o4: "RF-1080" has the value 1,080 and is number 2 of 4 in ascending order. Comparing digit by digit from the left puts it in the wrong place.
